newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina teacher withdraws resignation.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina teacher withdraws resignation.

text.p: A teacher who wrote "Where are my glasses!" on the face of a student decided on Sunday to withdraw her resignation and take her chances with the Charleston County School Board.
The board was to have its regularly scheduled meeting on Monday night.

In a statement issued on Sunday by her lawyer, Deena Smith McRackan, Phyllis Adelsflugel said she decided to withdraw the resignation "after much thought and prayer and after an incredible outpouring of support."
She said her decision to resign came under the "most intense pressure I have ever felt."

"I came to Charleston County with excellent recommendations," the statement said. "I have tried to demonstrate enthusiasm and innovation in my teaching, to be more than mediocre. I did not make a mistake of malice, but of enthusiasm."
Adelsflugel cleaned out her classroom on Saturday after agreeing to resign just before midnight Friday night. Several parents and their children as well as some teachers helped her.

On Saturday parents said they would continue their fight for the teacher by forcing a meeting with Charleston County School Superintendent Chip Zullinger, who they said ignored their requests for a meeting.
Adelsflugel told the parents that if she had not resigned, she would have been fired, jeopardising her teaching certificate, parents said.

Adelsflugel wrote the message on 5-year-old Nina Campbell's face on Nov. 13 and was suspended with pay the next day. The district's lawyers and administrators conducted a week-long investigation, culminating in a meeting with Adelsflugel and her lawyer, during which she resigned.

Nina Campbell's mother, Teresa, has alleged racism in the incident, saying the white teacher would not have done the same to a white child. Nina was transferred to another Charleston County school, which she attended for the first time on Friday.
Teresa Campbell is pressing for a law prohibiting teachers from writing "punitive messages" on children's faces.
